alt: The program counts every pair of positions with a nested loop. The outer loop picks a position i. The inner loop then adds one to count for each position after i, so it gets shorter as i grows.

Line 4 runs: the loop gives `i` its first value, `0`. `i` picks the first position of a pair. Each pass of this loop starts a fresh inner loop.
Line 5 runs: the loop gives `j` its first value, `1`. The inner loop starts at `i + 1`, so it runs fewer times every time `i` grows: 3, then 2, then 1, then 0 passes when n is 4.
Line 6 runs: `count` changes from `0` to `1`. Every pass through here counts one pair. Six passes in total for n = 4.
